LESSON: FEEDING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: My Family 2.1 Family members • father • mother • brothers • sisters • grandmothe
Topic 2.2: Feeding
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Feeding, part of My Family 2.1 Family members • father • mother • brothers • sisters • grandmothe in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we eat?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Feeding together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: learner develops confidence when is he or she is able to feed self-using clean hands appropriately.

Communication and Collaboration: learner speaks clearly and effectively when naming different foods.

Values:
Respect: as learner respect others opinions while talking about appropriate feeding habits.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Preventive health: learner enhances nutrition when feeding self appropriately.

• Financial literacy: learner finishes food as an appropriate feeding habit.

Link to other learning areas:

Feeding item can be used when doing matching and pairing feeding objects in Mathematical Activities

14

Charts, picture cards, clay, flash cards, drawn pictures of plate, spoon and food, glue, crayons, water containers, realia (plate, spoon), coloured

pencils, fruits, digital devices with assistive technology, different types of food, braille writing materials and equipment.
